188188:
Amanda Hartman In Support Of LD 1060 An Act to Provide Funding to Reduce Stigma for Parents Seeking
Suppon
April 3,2025
Good Morning, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee. My name is Amanda Hartman. Thank you for your
time and the opportunity to be heard. I am herein support of LD 1060.
Being a part of the Be There For Me campaign has been an incredibly rewarding experience. You might even recognize me as one ofthe faces ofthe campaign, perhaps on a poster or even a bus. I proudly stand by this campaign because I know that having a platform that is easy to navigate, user-friendly, and truly there for people in a supportive way makes sense. It's an honor to stand with the people working on this campaign to make this world more
supportive.
I have turned to so many agencies that are supposed to be our support systems, the ones meant to provide information, opportunities, education and understanding. Instead, I've been met with silence, left to navigate this complex web of life alone. It feels like you have
to fight a constant, exhausting battle just to access the help that is supposedly available.
You have to become your own full-time advocate, not only for yourself but your child and
your whole family, relentlessly pushing for a chance to improve your situation, even on days
when the sheer exhaustion makes it feel impossible. Doing everything for not only yourself
but your child/children and family, as well. All while not falling apart, not being sick or
having any new crisis to deal with.
So I ask: where do we turn? Where is the non-judgmental, genuinely helpful support that doesn't speak down to those of us struggling? Where are the resources that truly understand the impossible tightrope we walk every single day as parents'? That's everything the Be There For Me Campaign is and continues to be for those who are forced to do the leg work alone, but they've made it easier to navigate and user friendly. They've reminded the
world, and most importantly myself, it's ok to not be ok and there are resources to help.
I hope you will support this important resource that supports parents like me to navigate life's challenges. We need to be there for Maine families -- and this is one great way to do
that. Thank you.

My name is April Tardiff, and I live in Old Orchard Beach. I am here today, April 4,

2025, to testify in strong support of LD 1060.

As a parent, one of my biggest challenges has been finding a supportive environment where my 3-year-old son can thrive. My son was asked not to return to two different childcare centers. This was a devastating experience for my family--leaving us feeling lost, like I was a bad parent, and worst of all, making my
son feel like he was a bad child. We needed support. We needed resources.
This is why it's so critical to normalize the challenges toddlers face in childcare
settings. My family is not alone in this experience--many parents have children
who struggle to fit into traditional childcare models. We need to ensure that
families have access to developmental services and inclusive childcare options. High-energy toddlers are not a problem----they need understanding, support, and
access to centers that meet their needs so they, and their families, can thrive.

Asking for help is difficult, especially when you don't know where to turn. That's
why Be There For Me has been a saving grace. It provides an easy, quick, and
reliable place for parents to find the help they need. Everything about Be There
For Me is designed thoughtfully----from its messaging, which tells real stories of
Maine families, to its simple and visually accessible website that connects parents directly to the right resources. Parents don't have time to sit on hold or navigate complicated systems--we need clarity, ease, and options at our fingertips. Be
There For Me delivers exactly that.

As a Parent Ambassador, I've had the privilege of contributing to this campaign.
I've seen firsthand the dedication of those who built it, ensuring families across Maine can access support without barriers. This is exactly the kind of resource we
must continue to invest in.

I urge you to support LD 1060 so this vital work can continue---so more families can find the help they need, and more organizations can share their resources
with those who need them most.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

10041922:
Testimony: Cindy Seekins, a parent who has raised children with emotional and behavioral health concerns in support of LD 1060, April 4, 2025
Good morning Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee
DHHS and MCWAN partnered with parents and caregivers (this means the process was Family Driven) to develop the "Be There for ME" website which was launched in July 2024 as a response to the feedback from parents and community partners who identified stigma as the significant barrier to parents in reaching out for and receiving of support. I participated in the Be There for ME development campaign in my role as a parent who has raised children with behavioral health concerns and with also having the knowledge of the experiences of other parents in Maine as the Director of a Statewide Parent Support Network whose parent family peer staff provide 1:1 in home support to parents of children/youth with emotional and behavioral health concerns.
Our task was to help to increase awareness of existing resources, remove the stigma associated with asking for help and to promote seeking help as a strength. As a parent I have the lived experience of feeling the isolation, stigma and of being shamed and judged for my children who have emotional and behavioral health needs. I was not aware of any resources for support and then I saw a simple advertisement for a "support group for parents of children with special needs". I truly wanted to attend, but then I would have to face the stigma and shame. Because of that stigma, it took me many months to have the courage to put aside those feelings to attend this support group and when I did, I received that nonjudgmental support and validation that I was a good parent. In retrospect, if the wording of the advertisement had been more supportive and encouraging I likely would have attended much sooner.
Parenting children is the toughest job you can ever have. The Be There for ME website is a needed resource for parents and is very critical to help to meet the many needs of families today. I was so appreciative of the openness to the "wording used" that was kind and supportive and removed the stigma, shame, blame and judgment that would help parents like myself to want to reach out sooner for assistance. THAT IS EXACTLY what parents need to see and feel when finding resources to make them feel safe and to encourage them to take the next step sooner. The Be There for ME website makes it more normalized to actually reach out for help and to contact the resources listed which can easily be accessed from any parents' phone. Best yet, there are no "key words" you have to already know to enter on that site in search for what you need.
If you are looking for cost effective resources that also truly meet the needs of the many, Be There for ME website is that resource. Currently, families have few places to get the professional help their children and youth need when they need it because of all the lengthy waitlists. This website contains many resources that do not have waitlists and that could help families increase their natural supports while increasing the resiliency factors for the entire family. I strongly support and encourage you to support the cost-effective request for additional funding maintenance of the Be There for ME website.
Respectfully submitted,
Cindy Seekins
188190:
Testimony of Melissa Hackett Coordinator, Maine Child Welfare Action Network
In support of LD 1060, An Act to Provide Funding to Reduce Stigma for Parents Seeking Suppon
April 4, 2025
Senator ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the Health and
Human Services Committee. My name is Melissa Hackett. I am a policy associate with
Maine Children's Alliance and serve as the coordinator for the Maine Child Welfare Action
Network. I am offering testimony today in support of LD 1060.
The Be There for ME campaign was initiated from the Child Safety and Family Well-Being Plan when the short-term version was released in May 2023. The 131 S` Legislature
generously allocated $750,000 in one-time funding to develop a campaign and website to normalize the challenges of parenting and promote help-seeking and knowledge of
resources.
It quickly became much more than a campaign. MCWAN and DHHS worked in partnership
to outreach and recruit parents first to share their perspectives around the challenges families were facing, and then to inform the development of the campaign and website -
from start to finish. It became a true partnership. From the colors and the logo to the words we chose for the website, Be There for ME is deeply informed by the perspectives of the
diverse group of parents we worked with to develop, promote, and launch it. I am deeply
gratefulto these parents for sharing their expertise and time with us to get this right.
Being a parent is hard. And while every family is unique, being a parent is a universally
challenging one. It doesn't come with instructions, and too many families are left
navigating the experience of parenting alone, without social support or connection to
resources to help them along the way. if we want kids to be safe and supported, we need to
invest in their parents and their ability to provide that safety and stability. That starts with
meaning it when we say it's okay to ask for help. And it means showing up in all the small and big ways for them - without judgement - as community members and in our
professional roles.
To illustrate how too many families in Maine feel right now, I would share this story. During the focus groups to develop the campaign, we offered parents options forthe name. One I was very fond of was "A Village for ME." I was surprised when every parent and caregiver group we brought this to responded with a resounding "no" to the name. One parent reflected that everyone says there's a village when you become a parent, but it's not true, and that hurts. Another parent joked that they must not have gotten the phone number for

the village. Still another remarked that where they came from, there actually was a village of support that didn't exist here. I share this because I think many of us like the idea, and
have the belief, that there is a village of support for families in Maine.
It is an unfulfilled promise we have made. And it's time to make good on it. It starts by investing in parents and supporting them withoutjudgement - because life is hard and
everyone needs help sometimes. That is especially true for parents as they navigate their
own personal challenges and those they experience in their role as parents. A parent
partner has reminded me that I am also a parent, as I have often thought to take off that "hat" when I am in my professional role. But it's not that simple. I am always also a parent.
And I have struggled, as I think every parent has at some point, and felt embarrassed or
scared to reach out for help. We need to counteract this stigma and fear with support.
That starts with the messages of support and hope and connections to places to start to
reach out that Be There for ME offers. It is a small price to pay to support families feeling they can reach out for help sooner, and get the support they need, when and where they need it, to take care of themselves and their children. I hope you willjoin me in supporting
this important legislation. Thank you.
188189:
Melissa Harding, Waldo County Mom Of Four
in Support of LD 1060 An Act to Provide Funding to Reduce Stigma for Parents Seeking Suppofl
April 4,2025
Good morning, Senator lngwersen, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee. Thank you for the opportunity to be here today and share my testimony in support of LD 1060 as a mother, as a community member, and as a parent leader that works with parents from all over the state who struggle with access
to resources and support while navigating the challenges of everyday parenting.
The Be There For ME Campaign is so much more than a campaign. It is more than a
website. it is more than messaging and advertisements. It is a call to action to every
community here in Maine to change the way we support and show up for families. It is an answer to the cries for help from families raising children with no village who feel isolated, alone, and left behind. Families who are afraid to ask for help, families who are ashamed they cannot make ends meet, families who are navigating systems they are afraid of,
because they feeljudged or often punished with child welfare intervention for trying to access the very resources that are in place for these exact circumstances.
Being a parent is the hardest job in the world, and it has only gotten harder since Covid.
Isolation and lack of resources have families hanging on by a thread. The Be There For ME
Campaign is changing that by answering those cries for help, by validating those struggles with no judgement, by lifting the voices of parents and families and saying being a parent is HARD, and it is ok to say it, it is ok to feel it, and it is ok to ask for help.
This messaging is different because it was created by parents, in their own words, with their own stories, and therefore it is received differently by other parents hearing this message that they are not alone in this. I can't tell you how many parents have personally reached out through this campaign to tell me they needed this so badly, they needed to
hear it, they needed to see it, they needed to feel it. They did not feel so alone now.
We can do better as human beings to support families. We can stop turning a blind eye to
their struggles, we can stop judging circumstances we do not understand, we can stop
acting like there is nothing we can do because of funding. We can listen. We can continue to lift the voices of families through the Be There For ME Campaign. We can say we hear
your cries for help, and together we can create our own village, and stronger communities here in Maine. So, today I am asking you to vote in favor of LD 1060 and lift up and hear the
voices of families. Today I am asking you to be there for ME.

Seeking Support

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services

Senator Ingwersen, esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee, I am
Representative Michele Meyer, serving the people of southern Maine's District 150, all of Eliot and
parts of Kittery and South Berwick. I am honored to introduce LD 1060, An Act to Provide Funding to
Reduce Stigma for Parents Seeking Support.

We all care about the safety and well-being of Maine children. One very important way we can
demonstrate our care and concern for kids is by supporting their parents. I am proud of the support I
have offered in the development of Maine's Child Safety and Family Well-Being Plan, which
establishes a collective framework for keeping children safe by keeping families strong.

One core tenet of this plan is acknowledgement that parents face stigma and fear in reaching out for help, which represents a significant barrier to ensuring they can get the help they need, when they need
it, to care for themselves and their children.

Responding to the fear and stigma Maine parents face expressed about reaching out for and receiving
help, in 2023 the Department of Health and Human Services and the Maine Child Welfare Action
Network, began working together with parents and community partners to develop a campaign focused on normalizing the challenges of parenting and encouraging and connecting to opportunities to reach
out for support through a new website -- BeThereforME.org. Notably, the website is intentionally
streamlined, so it's not overwhelming for parents to navigate, and highlights places where parents can
talk to someone to support them in navigating possible supports.

Parent partnership is another core principle of the Plan, and this was demonstrated in the development
of Be There for ME. By working in partnership with parents, partners were able to produce a campaign
and website that reflects what parents say they need, in the ways and words they use to talk about their

own lives. The strength of Be There for ME is how much it was developed and informed by parents,
for parents. The campaign messages nonnalize the challenges of parenting universally and encourage seeking support. The website offers places to start to reach out for support across a variety of issues, including health care, food, child care, housing, and behavioral health.
Be There for ME was developed as part of a one-time $75 0,000 budget initiative in the 1315`
Legislature, after the first version of the Child Safety and Family Well-Being Plan was launched in
May of 2023.
This bill is a critical opportunity to ensure the foundation that has been established through the Be
There for ME campaign and website is sustained. The fiscal note reflects a modest investment in
ongoing paid promotion and website maintenance to ensure this. It is a small price to pay to make sure parents in Maine hear loud and clear the message that being a parent is hard, it's okay to ask for help,
and there is support out there. I hope you will join me in supporting this bill.

10042230:
Raychel Ward Livermore falls LD 1060
Hello, I am Raychel Ward a Maine State Parent Ambassador Alumni from Livermore Falls Maine. Being a parent in Maine is hard. Really hard. It seems like every system that is meant to helps us fails us and our children. Sometimes we do not know where else to turn. Sometimes we really need support and understanding to help us parent our children despite the challenges of finding proper childcare, protecting our children from dangerous people, sometimes even their relatives. Sometimes we just need someone to listen and actually understand. It can be hard to know what resources we have available to us. Bethereforme.org has been so helpful in not only providing support but making it easier to find the resources we need. It is important to normalize the fact that parents need support. It has been proven that well supported parents are less likely to abuse or neglect their children. In a state where our child protective services system has been failing for decades I cannot think of a reason more worth of funding and working towards having well supported parents. It is hard to ask for help because sometimes were afraid of the system because we have been the subject of unwarranted investigations. We need to be able to ask for help without fear of being subjected to suspicion that we have caused harm or will cause harm to our children. It is hard to find help because our many systems (Healthcare, mental health, children's behavioral health, special education, ect.) are already so taxed and heavily burdened it seems futile to keep trying. However, stopping is not an option if we want the best outcomes for our families. Be There For ME needs to be supported. Be There For ME is a resource that parents who are scared to ask for help are more likely to use because it is self service and user friendly. It connects us to other parents and services that support us and makes our communities better supported and stranger. It has been my honor to be a part of the campaign and support of parents all over the state of Maine in their parenting journey. Like any parent my goal is stable supported families and to promote the best outcomes for our children. Please vote ought to pass on LD1060

Dear Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, Representative Javner and the honorary members of the Health and Human Services Committee:
My name is Richard A. Hooks Wayman, and I am a resident of Portland, Maine. I have the honor of serving as the President & CEO for VOA Northern New England which is headquartered in Brunswick. VOA Northern New England is a faith-based, community nonprofit that works with households experiencing deep poverty, disabilities, and homelessness. I am also a foster-adoptive father to six children and a member of the Maine Child Welfare Action Network.
As a child advocate and a nonprofit director of housing and human services across Maine, VOA witnesses families impacted by deep poverty, disabilities, and the child protective system. For years we have asked that child welfare services move `upstream' to prevent child maltreatment. The Be There for ME is one of the most important system reforms Maine has undertaken in the past decade. As part of Maine's Child Safety and Family Well-Being Plan, child welfare experts, impacted families, and public officials at DHHS have recognized that the pathway to decreasing child neglect and maltreatment is to bolster the social and economic wellbeing of families and reduce the stigma of asking for help.
LD 1060 would offer continuing funding to reach families. In this modern, digital world we reach parents not only through word of mouth but through digital communication. Funding is needed to make critical updates to the DHHS Be There for Me website and conduct media promotion of the campaign. At $100,000 per year, this seems to be a low-cost, high-impact investment to support Maine children and families!
Thank you for considering my testimony. I am grateful for your public service and leadership.
Sincerely,
Richard A. Hooks Wayman, President & CEO VOA Northern New England

10042065:
Ryan Quinn Testimony in support of LD 1060, An Act to Provide Funding to Reduce Stigma for Parents
Seeking Support April 4, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the committee. My name is Ryan Quinn, a parent participant in the Be There For ME Campaign. I am o ering testimony today in support of LD 1060.
It was an honor and privilege to be considered and subsequently interviewed for the Be There for ME campaign. It is a very forward-thinking and very necessary resource that not only serves as a valuable public campaign, but also a wonderful resource hub, where parents and families can start to access supports for a variety of needs via a clean and easy to access website.
Being a parent or caregiver can be beautiful, rewarding, and life changing. What is not often discussed openly is that it can also be challenging, di icult, and isolating. Be There for ME as a campaign helps normalize drawing attention to these challenges that many parents and caregivers face in isolation. To me the campaign, through the integrated stories and media that accompany the information, speaks "that it's ok to say this is hard," "It's ok to ask for help," and "you are not alone." Whether it's mental health challenges, their child's mental health, housing, food, healthcare, or childcare, etc., a hub and campaign like Be There for ME o ers supports while validating the challenges that come with being a parent or caregiver. This can help reduce the stigma that often comes with asking for help.
I know this because not only am I a single parent that participated in the campaign, but I also am a Community Service Provider.
I work at The Opportunity Alliance in South Portland, ME - the Community Action Agency for Cumberland County. I can say firsthand that since the launch of the campaign, I have witnessed this resource quickly start to take hold and be shared between providers and is recommended as one of the first resources for many providers to share with families that they work with. It's rare that a week goes by where I don't overhear this campaign recommended or discussed, with most not even realizing I participated in the campaign. Whether in statewide provider meetings where resources are shared, or in my agency's own Community of Practice meetings, this is a resource that has quickly started to be integrated into Community Action. Additionally, this is a wonderful companion resource to the growing "Whole Family" approach that many Community Action Agencies are adopting philosophically.

It can take time for a new resource to take hold, catch wind, grow, and become "normalized" as a trusted resource. Be There for ME has already been able to largely achieve this in its infancy. Further supporting this work through LD 1060 will allow the team behind it to continue to expand and grow the resource to gain a further reach. Why is this important? When I think about this resource, I see it has an ability to operate as a preventative measure - to reduce stigma, and empower parents and caregivers to access information, resources, and supports proactively. That provides a critical opportunity to help prevent a di icult situation from becoming a crisis. That proactive support benefits children, families, and the communities they work and live in across our state. Thank you.
Ryan Quinn
